messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate in eu-west-1 (service: inference-proxy). Error spike started ~2026-03-15T05:12Z — paging on-call.
Maya: I got the page, jumping in. primary oncall for this shift here. putting a quick note in thread.
Arjun: On secondary, available for handoff. any initial customer impact notes?
Priya: Quick summary from logs: a subset of requests to model pool redacted-13 are returning 503 from proxy with `upstream read timeout / connection reset`. Looks correlated with host oom/killed on k8s nodes in eu-west-1.
Sam: I see the same in Grafana — p95 latency up 3x for eu-west, 5xx rate up ~12% in the last 15m. Errors concentrate on pods on node pool `gpu-eu-spot-2`.
Maya: ok — immediate plan: mark primary node pool as drained, scale new warm nodes in dedicated pool, and fail traffic to fallback region for high-priority customers. Follow runbook: `ops/runbooks/evict-failing-node.md` (short checklist below).
Priya: customer impact: two customers (acct-867, acct-420) reported retries from their side. No widespread alerts from billing, but API retries visible. Noting SLAs: medium risk if not mitigated in next 30-60m.
Arjun: I'll take drain/evict step. Maya you own routing/fallback policy changes?
Maya: Yep. I'll patch the routing policy to prefer `eu-central-1` for high-latency requests and enable soft-fallback on the proxy for the next 45m. Command I'll run:
```
# cordon + drain the bad node(s)
kubectl cordon gpu-node-23 --context=eu-west-1
kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# scale up warm pool
kubectl apply -f k8s/warm-pool-eu.yaml --context=eu-west-1
```
Sam: adding a guard: set `max_concurrency=1` for canary routes to reduce mem pressure while we stabilize.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: `release/2026.03.15.4` — patch to proxy with more resilient keepalive handling. CI passed.
Maya: good catch. I'll hold deploy until we confirm drain progress. Priya — can you validate evicted pods had large RSS before kill? paste sample logs if any.
Priya: pasted snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T05:09:45Z] pod/worker-7 PID=4321 OOMKilled, RSS=48GB vm=56GB model=redacted-13 seq=2048
[2026-03-15T05:10:01Z] proxy connection reset to 10.2.4.7: upstream read timeout
```
Maya: that points to model mem pressure at ~seq=2k for some requests. We'll temporarily reduce max sequence length on that pool to 1024 as a patch.
Arjun: I'll coordinate node replacements and watch autoscaler; also verifying spot eviction notices for those nodes. If they were spot preempted that's a different story.
Sam: I'm instrumenting a temporary histogram on `request.seq_len` to catch which requests are >1024.
Priya: Customer-facing note draft (for Maya to approve): "We're seeing elevated error rates in eu-west due to node-level memory pressure affecting a subset of heavy requests. We're failing over traffic and scaling replacement capacity; we'll provide updates every 30 minutes." :eyes:
Maya: LGTM. Post that in #general after we confirm routing change.
Arjun: Node cordon/drain started for gpu-node-23 and gpu-node-24. Both had recent spot termination warnings -> confirming with cloud logs now.
Maya: Routing patch applied to prefer eu-central for high-priority routes. Fallback policy enabled. Rolling window: 45m. Monitoring: dashboards are showing success rate rising slowly.
Sam: 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 3% in 10m since drain started. p95 latency trending down but still ~1.8x baseline.
Priya: I've flagged reqs >1024 tokens and stopped routing them into redacted-13 pool (temporary rule). That reduced RSS pressure on remaining pods.
Maya: Next: 1) continue warm-pool spin-up (Arjun) 2) validate deploy patch (hold until warm nodes registered) 3) follow-up customer note + postmortem owner assignment. Who wants postmortem?
Arjun: I can drive postmortem. I'll collect timeline, node events, and autoscaler logs.
Sam: I'll own observability follow-ups — add missing metrics for sequence length and pod RSS in the dashboard.
Priya: I'll work on customer comms and include a short mitigation timeline.
Maya: For next shift handoff (primary -> next): current primary=Maya until 10:00Z, secondary=Arjun. After 10:00Z, Sam will be primary and Priya secondary. Noting coverage gap between 14:00-15:00Z tomorrow; can we get a volunteer to cover that window? @Arjun can you confirm overlap for handoff tomorrow?
Arjun: I can cover 14:00-15:00Z tomorrow if needed. Marked in calendar.
Maya: Action items (short):
- Arjun: finish warm-pool + confirm spot eviction root cause (in progress)
- Sam: add seq_len & pod RSS charts, alert threshold for seq>1024
- Priya: publish 15:40Z customer update & maintain 30m cadence
- Maya: monitor routing fallback and approve deploy-bot patch once warm nodes healthy
- Arjun: postmortem lead
Everyone: react :thumbsup: when you have the item noted.
Priya: :thumbsup:
Sam: :thumbsup:
Arjun: :thumbsup:
Maya: :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Pager silenced by Maya for 60m (maintenance window). Reminder: escalate if errors > 10% sustained.
Maya: leaving a short log for the next oncall: drained nodes were spot preempted; RAM pressure likely from large seq requests. We reduced max-seq to 1024 on the pool and enabled region fallback. Warm pool scaling to complete in ~20m. Postmortem owner Arjun. Contact points: Priya (customers), Sam (obs), Arjun (postmortem/infra).
Arjun: noted. I'll attach cloud termination events and node metrics to the postmortem draft.
Sam: will add dashboard links and a quick runbook tweak: recommend adding `seq_len` histogram + alert. I'll open PR to runbooks.
Priya: posting the customer note now.
Maya: handing off — I'm still reachable for escalation but shifting primary role to Sam at 10:00Z. Good job team. :relieved:
Sam: taking primary at 10:00Z. I'll keep monitoring and update if anything flares.
